comments.author: bluedays
comments.story_title: A curated list of Computer Engineering resources
comments.why_zh: Abelson 谈计算机科学并非关于计算机
comments.quote_zh: 计算机科学其实并不真的是关于计算机的。
comments.text_zh: 你问得真巧，我正好在看 Harold Abelson 的一场讲座，他讲的正是这个问题。[VIDEO] 如果你没时间或没兴趣看视频，基本上可以这样概括。当埃及人最初发现几何学时，它被视为一门农作物科学，因为它的主要应用是确定作物产量以及何时播种和收割。同样地，如今计算机科学被应用在计算机上。但就像几何学实际上是关于农耕的，计算机科学其实并不真的是关于计算机的。Abelson 教授接着解释说，计算机科学提供了一种为抽象数学推理确定证明的手段，让我们能用确凿的证明去理解那些迄今为止只是理论的东西。
comments.text: It’s funny you should ask that as I was just watching a lecture by Harold Abelson in which he addresses this exact question. [VIDEO] In case you don’t have the time or inclination to watch the video it can basically be summarized by saying the following. When the Egyptians first discovered geometry it was considered crop science as it’s primary application was for determining crop yields and when to plant and harvest. In the same way now that computers science is applied to computers today. But just like Geometry is really about farming, computer science is not really about computers. Professor Abelson goes on to explain that computer science provides a means to determine proofs for abstract mathematics a reasoning, so that we can understand with definitive proof things that until now were only theoretical.

comments.author: arexxbifs
comments.story_title: Tribes of Programming (2017)
comments.why_zh: Abelson 谈计算机科学与计算机的关系
comments.quote_zh: 它不是关于计算机的，就像物理不是真的关于粒子加速器一样。
comments.text_zh: 不知道这个“玩笑”是不是 Abelson 和 Sussman 首创的，但这里是 Hal Abelson 谈到它时的说法：（ [VIDEO] ）“它不是关于计算机的，就像一个物理学家并不是真的在研究粒子加速器一样。”我有点同意，但我想这取决于我们所说的计算机科学是关于计算机的到底是什么意思。我们现在能做到一些在 A&S 录制他们的 Lisp 讲座时根本不可能做到的事，仅仅是因为我们可以换一种方式思考在时间和空间复杂度方面什么是合理的。当然，Abelson 本人在后来的一次讲座中还开玩笑说，每个人都想要更快的计算机。也许我们只是把计算机科学和软件开发搞混了，我想这可以类比为把数学和会计搞混。
comments.text: Don't know if the "joke" originated with Abelson and Sussman but here's Hal Abelson talking about it: [VIDEO] "It's not about computers in the same sense that physics is not really about particle accelerators." I sort of agree, but I guess it depends on what we mean about computer science being about computers. We can do things now that were downright impossible when A&S recorded their Lisp lectures simply because we can think differently about what's reasonable with regards to time and space complexity. And, of course, Abelson himself jokes about everyone wanting a faster computer in a later lecture. Perhaps we're simply confusing CS with software development, which I suppose could be likened to confusing mathematics with accounting.
